requests.original_text: If, under the term " subject," you had included the scope and design of the writer, it had been so far good; but, by this term, you ap- pear all along to mean, the doctrine of future punishment, abstract- edly considered from what the scriptures teach concerning it; at least, from what they teach by the terms which professedly denote its duration.

requests.original_text: When I sug- gested that " the nature of the subject determined that the term everlasting, when applied to future punishment, was to be taken in the endless sense," I intended no more, than that such is the sense in which it is used when applied to a future state.

requests.original_text: By your rule of interpretation, I have the '^ temerity" to say again, you might disprove almost any thing you please. 1 observed before, that if one should attempt to prove the divinity of the Son of God, or even of the Father, from his being called /eAoi;aA, your mode of reasoning would render all such evidence of no account ; because the same appellation is sometimes given to an altar, &c.

requests.claim: 예수 그리스도가 주님으로 불려도 그것만으로는 그를 참된 하나님으로 믿을 수 없다.

requests.original_text: You answer, " The question ought not to be, what language God could have used; but, what is the meaning of that which he has
requests.claim: 하나님의 말씀의 의미를 이해하는 것이 중요하다

requests.original_text: Should this be the case, it must follow that, if they do not convey the idea of endless duration, it is not in the power of language, or, at least, of that language, to convey it.
requests.claim: 어떤 용어가 무한한 기간을 전달하는 아이디어를 전달하지 않는다면, 그것은 언어의 한계 또는 그 언어의 한계 때문이다.

requests.original_text: I can form no idea how the term indissoluble, any more than incorrupti- ble, can apply to punishment The word xaTaXiJW, to unloose, or dissolve, is true, is said to refer to travellers loosing their own burdens, or those of their beasts, when they are resting by the way: but there are no examples of its having been used with ref- erence to the termination of punishment; nor does it appear to be applicable to it.
requests.claim: 형벌에 대한 '해결할 수 없는'이라는 용어의 적용 가능성에 대한 의문

requests.original_text: In its most common acceptation in the New Testament, it signifies to destroy, or demolish; and you will scarce-
requests.claim: xaTaXiJW라는 단어는 일반적으로 파괴나 해체를 의미한다

requests.original_text: ly suppose the sacred writers to suggest the idea of a destruction which cannot be destroyed.
requests.claim: 성경의 저자들은 파괴될 수 없는 파괴의 아이디어를 제안한다.

requests.original_text: And are the Greek words there used, stronger than a/wv, and its derivatives ?
requests.claim: 에페소서 3:21에 사용된 그리스어 단어가 a/wv와 그 파생어보다 강한가?

requests.original_text: Had these very terms been applied to future punishment, you would have pleaded for a different translation, and denied that they were expressive of endless duration.
requests.claim: 특정한 용어들이 미래의 형벌에 적용되었다면, 다른 번역을 주장하였을 것이며, 그 용어들이 무한한 지속을 의미한다는 것을 부정하였을 것이다.

requests.original_text: The amount of your first maxim, in p. 330, appears, to me, to be this : ' That if God created men, and placed them in circumstances which he certainly foreknew would issue in their fall and ruin, he willed this their fall and ruin ; and this is of no importance thai he forewarned them to avoid the evil : whatever be the event, he is chargeable with it.' ' But God,' you say, ' hath sworn by him- self, that he willeth not the death of him who dieth ; that is, he willeth it not as death finally or simply, or destruction irrecovera- ble.
requests.claim: 하나님의 섭리와 인간의 자유의지 사이의 관계는 하나님의 의지와 인간의 선택 사이의 상호작용을 포함한다

requests.original_text: If, therefore, it occur, it is a part of his economy of grace, and, finally, a ministration unto life ; for he hath declared, it is hi§
requests.claim: 하나님의 경제는 그분의 은혜의 일부로 작동하며, 궁극적으로는 생명으로 향하는 사역이다.

requests.original_text: will that all should be saved : therefore, the doctrine which for- ges any contrary will, falsifies supreme, unchangeable truth.'
requests.claim: 하나님의 의지는 모든 사람이 구원받기를 원한다

requests.original_text: Let the blasphemer make what use he may of it, it may be asked, Who hath resisted his will ?
requests.claim: 하나님의 의지에 반대하는 것은 없다.

requests.original_text: The good that shall arise from it, and not the evil, is the proper object of divine volition.
requests.claim: 하나님의 의지는 악을 원하는 것이 아니라, 악이 존재하는 것을 허락하며, 그로부터 나온 선을 원한다.

requests.original_text: But it is not true, that God is on this account chargeable with man's sin ; that all his cautions and warnings are of no account ; and that he is to be *' accused'" of the death of the sinner, if he die eternally.
requests.claim: 하나님의 의지는 인간의 죄에 책임을 지우지 않는다

requests.original_text: If it be, however, it is not the doctrine of Universal Salvation that will free him from the charge.
requests.claim: 만물의 구원에 관한 교리는 하나님을 인간의 죄에 대한 책임에서 자유롭지 못하게 한다.

requests.original_text: It is a fact, (is it not ?) that God did place man in circumstances which he certainly foreknew would issue in his fall ; and that he did, notwithstanding, caution and warn him against apostasy, and still continues to caution and warn sinners against those very sins which he certainly foreknows they will commit : Who, then, is this that dares to arraign his conduct, and to accuse him of insincerity ? — Who, that, at one stroke, aims to sweep away the accoutableness of his creatures ; and to charge him with the evil of their sin, on account of his having placed them in such circumstances ?
requests.claim: 하나님은 인간이 반드시 타락하는 것을 예견하면서도 인간을 타락으로부터 경고하였고, 여전히 죄인들을 그들이 저지르게 될 죄로부터 경고하셨다.

requests.original_text: If it be as you insinuate, it must follow, that man is not blame- worthy in all his rebellion against his Maker, nor justly accounta- ble for any of its consequences.
requests.claim: 만약 인간의 반역이 그의 창조주에 대한 책임이 없다면, 인간은 자신의 모든 반역에 대해 책임을 지지 않을 것이며, 그 결과에 대한 책임도 지지 않을 것이다.

requests.original_text: Let no man say, when he is tempted^ I am tempted of God.
requests.claim: 하나님은 우리를 시험하는 것이 아님을 주장한다.

requests.original_text: Yes, says Mr. Vidler, it is he, who, knowing all events, and placing us in such circumstances as he does, that is accountable I And it is of no importance, m the consideration of common sense, that he cautions, or forewarns, us against the evil.
requests.claim: 하나님이 모든 사건을 아시고 우리를 특정한 상황에 두심으로써, 하나님은 우리의 시험에 대한 책임을 지신다.

requests.original_text: If what you have suggested be true, it must also follow, that there is no need of a mediator, or of forgiving mercy.
requests.claim: 중재자나 용서의 자비가 필요하지 않다.

requests.original_text: If the Creator only to be accountable for the evil, it belongs to him to remedy it.
requests.claim: 만물의 창조주가 악에 책임을 지는 경우, 악을 치료하는 것은 창조주에게 속하는 일이다.

requests.original_text: " He sent his children into the wood, it seems, where he knew the poisonous fruit abounded j .and though he warned them against it, yet he was not in earnest ; and when they had eaten, to the endangering of their lives, he counteracted the poison ; but was conscious, at the same time, that, if there were any fault in the affair, it was his own ; and if the children were to perish, he would be justly accused of their death." And can you, Sir, with these sentiments, continue to dis- avow your invalidating the divine three tenings towards sinners ^ and concurring with him who taught our first parents, " Ye shall not surely die ?" What better exposition could the deceiver of mankind have wished for, than what your words afford !
requests.claim: 하나님의 경고와 경고는 진정성이 없으며, 인간의 죄는 하나님의 책임이다.

requests.original_text: " If death occur, it is a part of his economy of grace, and finally a ministration unto life." That is, it shall prove a benefit.
requests.claim: 죽음이 발생하더라도 그것은 하나님의 은혜의 경제학의 일부이며, 궁극적으로는 생명으로 향하는 섬김으로 증명될 것이다.

requests.original_text: That is, he willeth it not as death finally, or simply, or de- struction irrecoverable." Death simply and finally, then, means irrecoverable destruction, does it ?
requests.claim: 하나님은 죽음 자체를 원하지 않으시며, 죽음은 궁극적으로 회복할 수 없는 파멸을 의미한다.

requests.original_text: First : The greater part of it is mere trifling. — Whoever sup- posed, that eternal punishment, or any punishment, was a benefit to God ; or even a pleasure to him, or any holy beings, for its own sake ?
requests.claim: 영원한 형벌이나 다른 형벌이 하나님께 이익이 되거나, 하나님이나 거룩한 존재들에게 그 자체로 즐거움을 주는 것은 아님

requests.original_text: Secondly : Some parts of it which object to endless punishment, because it cannot be for the honour of God, or the bene^t of crea-
requests.claim: 무한한 형벌은 하나님의 영광이나 창조물의 이익에 부합하지 않는다.

requests.original_text: Was safety the only end answered to the world by the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrha ; or were they not rather set forth for an example?
requests.claim: 소돔과 고모라의 멸망은 세계에 안전을 제공하는 것 이상의 목적을 가지고 있다.

requests.original_text: Is it only for the safety of society, ti)at a mur- derer is publicly executed ?
requests.claim: 범죄자를 공개적으로 처형하는 것은 사회의 안전뿐만 아니라, 좋은 정부가 범죄에 대한 불쾌감을 표현하고, 대중의 마음에 그것을 각인시키는 예를 보여주는 데에도 필요하다.

requests.original_text: That end would be equally answer- ed by perpetual imprisonment, or banishment, or \\ private execu- tion : but there would be wanting an example, to express the dis- pleasure of a good government against crimes, and to impress the public mind with it.
requests.claim: 사형은 사회의 안전을 위한 수단이지만, 또한 정부가 범죄에 대한 불쾌감을 표현하고 대중의 마음에 영향을 미치는 예시로서의 역할을 한다.

requests.original_text: Thirdly : Most of what you say on this subject, if admitted, would overturn all future punishment.
requests.claim: 대부분의 당신의 주장이 받아들여진다면, 모든 미래의 형벌을 뒤엎을 것이다.

requests.original_text: You might ask, Would it be honourable to God, to have any of his creatures miserable/or ages of ages, rather than happy ?
requests.claim: 하나님의 창조물이 영원토록 불행한 것보다 행복한 것이 하나님께 영광이다.

requests.original_text: As to the punished, future punishment can be neither honour nor" pleasure to them : and, if their salvation could be accomplished without it, it cannot be any benefit to them.
requests.claim: 형벌을 받는 자들에게 미래의 형벌은 영광이나 즐거움을 줄 수 없으며, 그들의 구원을 위해 그것이 필요하지 않다면, 그것은 그들에게 어떤 이익도 될 수 없다.

requests.original_text: If they may not be saved without it, it must be either because there was not eflScacy
requests.claim: 구원받기 위해서는 반드시 형벌을 받아야 하며, 그 형벌이 없이는 구원은 불가능하다.

requests.original_text: enough in the blood of Christ for the purpose; or else, that " the full efficacy of the atonement was withheld by the divine deternni- nation." As to fellozv-creatures, can the future punishment of any of the human race be any honour to them ?
requests.claim: 그리스도의 피에는 충분한 효력이 있으며, 하나님의 결정에 의해 속죄의 완전한 효력이 제한될 수 있다.

requests.original_text: Who ever thought it an honour to him, that any of his family were punished in any way ?
requests.claim: 가정 구성원의 처벌은 명예가 아니다

requests.original_text: Is it not a dishonour to humm nature at large to be sent to hell ?
requests.claim: 지옥에 보내짐은 인간 본성 전체에 대한 치욕이다.

requests.original_text: Can any creature have pleasure in the punishment of another ?
requests.claim: 어떤 창조물도 다른 존재의 처벌에서 기쁨을 느끼지 않는다.

requests.original_text: Would not every benevolent mind possess a greater pleasure in seeing sinners converted and saved, without going to hell ; than 1.0 see them condemned to weeping and wailing and gnashing of ieeihj for ages of ages ?
requests.claim: 자비로운 마음을 가진 모든 사람은 죄인들이 지옥에 가지 않고 회개하고 구원받는 것을 보는 것에 더 큰 기쁨을 느낄 것이다.

requests.original_text: As, then, future torments can answer no possible good end to any one in the universe, I conclude them to he neither the work nor will of God ; and, consequently, not the doctrine of scripture !
requests.claim: 미래의 고난은 우주에서 누구에게도 가능한 좋은 목적을 달성하지 못하므로, 그것은 하나님의 작품이나 의지라고 결론지을 수 없으며, 따라서 성경의 교리는 아니다.

requests.original_text: "Sin and misery," you say, "have no root or foundation in God;" and, therelore, must come to an end.
requests.claim: 죄와 고통은 하나님께 근거를 두지 않으므로 결국 끝나야 한다.

requests.original_text: Reduce your argument to form, and see what it will amount to : — Whatever has its root in the creature must come to an end : But sin and misery have their root in the creature : Therefore sin and misery must come to an end : Now what proof, I ask, have you for your major proposition ?
requests.claim: 죄와 고통은 창조물에 뿌리를 두고 있기 때문에 끝나야 한다.

requests.original_text: If, instead of taking our religion from the Bible, we labour to form a system from our own ideas of fitness and unfitness, and interpret the Bible accordingly, there will be no end of our wan- derings.
requests.claim: 성경을 따라 신앙을 세우지 않고, 오히려 자기 생각에 따라 신앙을 형성하고 성경을 해석하면, 그 잘못된 길에 빠진 결과는 끝이 없을 것이다.

requests.original_text: To this I answer, First : If it be owing to the mediation of Christ, that punishment should be a work of mercy, tliis is allowing, that if no mediator had been provided, it must have been the reverse.
requests.claim: 중보자 없이 죄에 대한 처벌은 자비가 아닌 다른 근거에서 비롯된다.

requests.original_text: But, if so, all your arguments against eternal punishment from the divine perfections, and all your at- tempts to maintain that the original meaning of the divine threat- enings never included this idea, are given up.
requests.claim: 중재자 없이 영원한 처벌은 하나님의 속성과 모순된다

requests.original_text: The " execution of judgment" committed to the Son, denotes, not merely the carrying into exe- cution the sentence at the last day, but the general administration of God's moral government, both in this world and that which is to come.
requests.claim: 그리스도께서 중보자로서 행하는 모든 일은 아버지께 왕국을 넘길 때 끝나며, 의인들의 상과 악인들의 벌도 그 시기에 끝나며, 그리스도는 한쪽을 주시고 다른 쪽을 내리실 것임

requests.original_text: You talk of our '' ascribing a proper eternity to sin and misery," as ifwe considered sin and misery to be necessarily eternal.
requests.claim: 죄와 고통을 필연적으로 영원한 것으로 간주하지 않는다.

requests.original_text: respect to creatures, are not necessarily eternal, any more than sin and misery ; and, in this view, it would be as improper to ascribe eternity to the purity and blessedness of the saved, as to the sin and misery of the lost, seeing, that the endless duration of both depends upon the will of God.
requests.claim: 신의 뜻에 따라 창조물의 상태는 영원하지 않을 수 있으며, 구원받은 자의 순수함과 복음과, 멸망한 자의 죄와 고통의 영원한 지속도 신의 뜻에 달려 있다.

requests.original_text: You speak of the "life and bles- sedness of holy beings, as having their root and foundation in God ; and that, being thus grounded in him, they will be, like him; eternal in duration." But this position is contrary to fact ; for was not " God the source and proper spring, both of the life and blessedness" of the unsinning angels ?
requests.claim: 신성한 존재들의 삶과 복된 상태는 하나님께 근거를 두고 있지만, 그들의 영원한 지속은 하나님의 의지에 달려있다

requests.original_text: The life and bles- sedness of man in a state of innocence, had their origin in God, as well as those of saints and angels ; yet they were not, on this ac- count, like their Author, "eternal in duration." To make such an assertion is, '^ to say the least of it, an unguarded mode of ex- pression:" but, more than this, it is contrary to fact, and tends to lessen the dependence of creatures upon God as the constant au- thor of all their happiness.
requests.claim: 인간의 생명과 복된 상태는 하나님께서 비롯되었지만, 그 본질이 영원한 것은 아님

requests.original_text: *' Sin and misery being contrary to the holiness and benevolence of God, they must (it seems) come to an end." Such an assertion is soon made: but where is the proof?
requests.claim: 신과 불행은 하나님의 거룩함과 선하심에 반대되므로, 그것들은 끝나야 한다.

requests.original_text: A little more assurance might lead another to say, that sin and misery, being contrary to the holiness and benevolence of God, cannot exi^t in a future state ; and, were it not for the awful evidence of facts, another might assert, that sin and misery do not now exist; for, in theory, it would be as easy to prove, that the present existence of sin and misery is as contrary to the holiness and benevolence of God, as their existence in future ; and that their existence, in future, /or ages of ageSf is as contrary to the holiness and benevolence of God, as their existence to an endless duration.
requests.claim: 죄와 고통은 하나님의 거룩함과 선하심에 반대되므로, 미래 상태에서 존재할 수 없을 것이라고 주장할 수 있다.

requests.original_text: unwary path, by measuring the divine administration by his own unhallowed notions of moral fitness.
requests.claim: 하나님의 섭리를 인간의 도덕적 관념으로 판단할 때 잘못된 길을 걸을 수 있다.

requests.original_text: If your attempts to prove that all judgment is a work of mercy, and yet that there may be judgment without mercy, should prove fruitless, it is no more than may be expected ; for the thing itself is a contradiction.
requests.claim: 모든 판단은 자비의 작품이지만, 자비 없이도 판단이 있을 수 있다.

requests.original_text: " The scriptures afford instances of punishment and pardon to the same persons, and for the same sins :"* but was this punishment without mercy?
requests.claim: 성경은 같은 사람과 같은 죄에 대해 벌과 용서의 예를 제공한다

requests.original_text: "Judgment and mercy were united in God's dealings with Jerusalem."!
requests.claim: 하나님의 예루살렘에 대한 처사는 심판과 자비가 결합된 것이었다.

requests.original_text: I should think, therefore, that this inheritance, of which the New Testament speaks very fully, cannot be said to be connected with successive duration ; not so connected, however, as to be commensurate with it.
requests.claim: 신약 성경에서 말하는 유업은 연속적인 시간과 관련이 있지 않다.

requests.original_text: Strictly speaking, it may be true, that the idea of successive duration necessarily attaches, and ever will attach, to the existence of creatures ; and that none but God can be said to exist without it : but there is a period, by your own acknowledgment, when the states of creatures will be for ever fixed ; and it^, at this period, sinners be doomed to everlasting pun- ishment, the term " everlasting" must be understood to mean end- less duration This period I conceive to be at the last judgment : you extend it to ages beyons! it.
requests.claim: 창조물의 존재는 필연적으로 연속적인 지속을 수반하며, 오직 하나님만이 이러한 연속성 없이 존재할 수 있다.

requests.original_text: This earth (which is to be the hell of wicked men, 2 Pet. iii. 7 — 13.) is to be renewed, whereby hell itself will be no more."* If the gloss will bear the test, you have certainly, for once, hit upon a clear proof of your point ; for none can imagine the con- flagration to be eternal.
requests.claim: 지구는 악한 사람들의 지옥이 될 것이며, 지옥은 더 이상 존재하지 않을 것이라고 주장한다.

requests.original_text: But this cannot be upon earth ; as its present condition does not admit of it.
requests.claim: 지구의 현재 상태는 지옥이 존재할 수 없음을 의미한다.

requests.original_text: You plead the promise, that " every knee shall bow to Christ," and consider this as inconsistent with ^' a stubborn knee, even in hell.' But the question is, Whether the bowing of the knee to Christ be necessarily expressive of a voluntary and holy submissiort to him ?
requests.claim: 크리스토에게 무릎을 꿇는 것이 반드시 자발적이고 거룩한 복종을 의미하는 것은 아니다.

requests.original_text: '^ All things," you allege, " are to be reconciled to the Father by the blood of the cross : but, while any continue in enmity against God, this can never be performed." (p. 364.) You refer, I suppose, to Col. i. 19, 20.
requests.claim: 십자가의 피로 모든 것이 아버지께로 화해되어야 하지만, 하나님께 대하여 적의를 지닌 사람들이 계속 존재하는 한, 이것은 결코 수행될 수 없다.

requests.original_text: '^ Christ," 3'ou add, '^ is to rule till his enemies are subdued; till there be no authority, power, or dominion, but what shall be sub- servient to him ; and, as the wages of sin is death, the second death must be here included." (p. 365.) This language, which is taken from 1 Cor. xv. is manifestly used in reference to the res- urrection of the bodies of those that sleep in Jesus, which is an event that precedes the last judgment ; for when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption — then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written.
requests.claim: 그리스도는 그의 적들이 복종할 때까지 다스리며, 그의 복종을 받지 않는 권위나 권세가 없을 때까지 그의 임무를 수행하며, 죄의 대가는 사망이므로, 두 번째 사망도 포함되어야 한다.

requests.original_text: And then cometh the end, the last judgment, and the winding up of all things, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God even the Father ; when he shall have put down all rule, and all authority, and power, (ver, 24, 25.) For you to interpret this language, of things that are to follow the last judgment, and to say that it must include the second death, proves nothing, but the dire necessity to which your system reduces you.
requests.claim: 마지막 심판과 모든 것의 종말은 하나님 아버지께 왕국을 넘길 때에 이루어지며, 모든 권위와 권력을 무너뜨릴 때에 이루어진다.

requests.original_text: *' Finally : the character of God is love; which is expressly against the horrible idea of the endless misery of any of his rational creatures." (p. 395.) So, Sir, you are pleased to assert.
requests.claim: 하나님의 성품은 사랑이므로, 그의 합리적인 창조물들 중 누구도 끝없는 고통에 빠지지 않는다.

requests.original_text: Is it inconsistent with the benevolence of a su- preme magistrate, that he dooms certain characters to death ?
requests.claim: 가장 높은 판결자가 특정 인물들을 죽음에 처하는 것은 그의 선행과 일치하지 않는다.

requests.original_text: Rather, is it not an exercise of his benevolence ?
requests.claim: 가장 높은 판결자가 특정한 자들을 죽음에 내모는 것은 그의 선행에 모순되지 않는다.

requests.original_text: Nay ; would it not be inimical to his own interest, and that of his fellow criminals ; as by raising a delusive hope, they are prevented from making a proper and timely application to the throne for mercy ?
requests.claim: 남자들이 자신의 죄를 인식하고 왕의 자비를 구하는 것을 방해하는 것은 그들의 이익과 동료 범죄자의 이익에 반대된다.

requests.original_text: You say, " If any be finally incorrigible, it must be in conse- quence of the divine purpose ; or else ihe purpose of God has been fustrated." I have in my last letter, replied to the substance of this dilemma.
requests.claim: 하나님의 목적이 실패할 수 없다는 점은 인정하지만, 일부 사람들의 최종적인 고집된 상태는 하나님의 목적의 결과일 수밖에 없다.

requests.original_text: I may add, you need be under no apprehen- sion, that I shall be tempted to give up the infrustableness of the divine purpose ; and if I admit, that God, in just judgment, has purposed to give some men up to stumble, and fall, and perish, it is no more than the scriptures abundantly teach.
requests.claim: 하나님의 목적은 불변하며, 하나님은 정의로운 판단으로 일부 사람들을 넘어지게 하고, 실패하게 하며, 멸망하게 하도록 작정할 수 있다.

requests.original_text: You talk of *^ the LAST state of a creature according with the divine purpose :" but I know of no evidence for this, which does not equally apply to every state.
requests.claim: 신의 목적에 따라 창조물의 마지막 상태를 결정하는 데 필요한 증거는 모든 상태에 동일하게 적용된다.

requests.original_text: Akin to this is your dilemma, " That God cannot, or will not, make an end of sin ; that there is not efficacy enough in the blood of Christ, to destroy the works of the devil ; or else, that the full efficacy of the atonement is withheld b}' the divine determination."
requests.claim: 하나님의 능력이나 의지로 인해 죄를 끝장내지 못하거나, 그리스도의 피의 효력이 마귀의 작품을 파괴하기에 충분하지 않거나, 속죄의 완전한 효력이 신의 결정으로 인해 제한된다.

requests.original_text: It has been already observed, and I hope proved, that the scrip- ture phrases, making an end of sin^ 8fc, convey no such idea as you attach to them. (p. 264.) And as to your dilemma, to which you ascribe great " weight," I. answer again, you need be under no apprehensions of my limiting the power of God, or the effica- cy of the Saviour's blood ; and, if I say, that both the one and the other are applied under the limitation of his own infinite wisdom, I say, not only what the scriptures abundantly teach, but what you yourself must admit.
requests.claim: 성경 구절이 말하는 죄의 종말은 특정한 의미를 내포하지 않는다.

requests.original_text: Can you pretend, that your scheme rep- resents God as doing all he can do, and as bestowing all the mercy which the efficacy of the Saviour's blood has rendered consistent ?
requests.claim: 하나님의 계획이 모든 사람을 구원하는 것인지에 대한 질문

requests.original_text: If so you must believe that God cannot convert more than he ac- tually does in the present life, and that the efficacy of the blood of Christ is not equal to the saving of more than a part of man- kind from the second death.
requests.claim: 하나님의 능력과 그리스도의 보혈의 효능은 현재의 삶에서 하나님이 실제로 회심시키는 사람의 수와 제2의 죽음으로부터 구원받는 사람의 수에 한정되어 있다.

requests.original_text: You think, that 'Hhe scripture is not silent concerning the fu- ture emendation of the ancient Sodomites ;" and refer me to Ezek. xvi. 44 — 63 j arguing, that " Sodom and her daughters must be taken hterally for the city of Sodom, and the neighboring cities of the plain ; that the prophecy must refer to the very per- sons who were destroyed, seeing they left no descendants ; and that there is the same reason to expect the restoration of Sodom, as the fulfilment of God's gracious promises towards Jerusalem." (p. 368. j But, if your interpretation prove any thing, it will prove — I will not say, too much, but too little.
requests.claim: 에스겔 16:44-63은 소돔과 그 딸들의 미래 개선에 대해 말하고 있다

requests.original_text: It will prove, not that the ancient Sodomites will be saved from " the vengeance of eternal fire," and introduced into the heavenly world; but, bare- ly, that they are to return to their former estate, (ver. 56.) And do you seriously think, that, after the last judgment, the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha, of Samaria and Jerusalem, will be rebuilt, and repossessed by their ancient inhabitants ?
requests.claim: 에스겔 16:44-63의 예언은 소돔과 고모라의 옛 주민들이 마지막 심판 후에 그들의 도시를 재건하고 재소유할 것이라는 것을 의미하지 않는다.

requests.original_text: in effect, not to expect it, any more than the former.* The lat- er part (ver. 60 — b'3.) contains the language of free mercy ; not however, towards the same individuals against whom the threat- nings are directed, but to their distant posterity, who, under the gospel dispensation, should be brought home to God; and by a new and better covenant, have the Gentiles given to them.
requests.claim: 구원은 자유로운 자비의 언어로 표현되며, 구원 약속은 경고를 받은 개인들이 아니라 그들의 먼 후손에게 주어지며, 복음의 섭리 아래 하나님께로 돌아오게 되고, 새로운 더 나은 언약으로 이방인들이 그들에게 주어진다.

requests.original_text: You " have not discernment enough, it seems, to perceive the gross absurdity" of maintaining that there can be no diversity in future punishment, unless it be in duration ; that is, that the reflec- tions of sinners on their past life must all be exactly the same.
requests.claim: 미래의 형벌에서 다양성이 없다면, 그것은 지속 시간에만 있는 것이어야 한다는 주장은 부조리하다.

requests.original_text: Your answer amounts to this : Diversity of degrees in future punishment may be accounted for, by varying the duration of it ; *' for every one knows there needs not so much time to inflict a hundred stripes, as to inflict ten times that number." Therefore, that must be the way, and the only way ; and if you do not admit it, you ^' confound all degrees of punishment, in giving infinite punishment to all." (pp. 42. 264. 369.)
requests.claim: 미래의 형벌의 정도 차이는 그 기간의 차이로 설명될 수 있다.

requests.original_text: You believe, you say, '^' those who die in their sins cannot go where Christ is." You must mean to say merely, that they cannot follow hiniTsioWy but shall follow fefm afterwards.
requests.claim: 그리스도께서는 죄 가운데 죽는 자들은 그분이 계신 곳으로 갈 수 없다고 믿는다고 말합니다. 그러나 이는 죄인들이 그리스도를 따라가지 못할 뿐이며, 나중에 따를 것이라는 뜻으로 이해해야 합니다.

requests.original_text: Such things. indeed, are said of Christ's friends, but not of his enemies.
requests.claim: 그리스도의 친구에게는 이러한 것들이 말해지지만, 그의 적들에게는 말해지지 않는다.

requests.original_text: You have represented me as maintaining, that all punishment clashes with the benevolence "both of God and his people." I have said no such thing concerning God: and if we were equally wise and righteous, and equally concerned to guard the interests of the universe, as he is, we should be, in all respects, of the same mind with him.
requests.claim: 진정한 선행은 고통을 가하는 것과 충돌한다.

requests.original_text: enemies, to do all in our power to preserve their lives, and save their souls : but He is not obliged to do all that he can to these ends, nor does he.
requests.claim: 하나님은 우리에게 적들을 위해 모든 것을 하도록 요구하지만, 하나님 자신은 그와 같은 의무를 지니고 있지 않다.

requests.original_text: Temporary punishment, you contend, may consist with benevolence, ^' because it is directed to a good and glorious end :" and do I contend for endless punishment on any other principle ?
requests.claim: 잠시 동안의 벌이 선하고 영광스러운 목적을 위해 존재할 수 있다

requests.original_text: If you can form no idea of an end that is good and glorious, save that which respects " the amendment of the sufferer," it does not follow that no such end exists.
requests.claim: 형벌의 목적이 고통받는 자의 개선에만 있는 것이 아니라는 것
